day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Vatican City/Borgo district via Leonardo Express train to Termini then Metro Line A to Ottaviano (~45 min, ~€20 total). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the Tiber River embankment and explore the Borgo district on foot. Visit the free exterior of Castel Sant'Angelo and walk across the iconic Ponte Sant'Angelo to admire the angel statues. Explore the charming narrow streets of Borgo Pio — a pedestrian lane lined with cafes and artisan shops, completely free to wander.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Piazza San Pietro (St. Peter's Square) at dusk for a magical, crowd-free atmosphere as the sun sets behind the basilica. The square is free to enter at any hour. Enjoy the illuminated colonnade and take in your first iconic Roman evening.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a quick coffee and cornetto at the airport before landing (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, affordable lunch near the hotel — try 'Il Sorpasso' or any local alimentari (deli) on Borgo Pio for a panino and water (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium-style meal at 'Pizzarium Bonci' on Via della Meloria (10 min walk) — Rome's legendary pizza al taglio (by the slice), sold by weight. Expect to spend €8–12 for a satisfying dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for airport transit. Validate your metro/bus tickets — inspectors are common. The Borgo district is very walkable and safe in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, opens 7:00 AM). Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Marvel at Michelangelo's Pietà, the grand nave, and Bernini's baldachin. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 by stairs, €10 by elevator — stairs recommended for budget travelers). Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. Book tickets online in advance to skip the line (~€20 general admission — the single biggest must-spend of the trip). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling by Michelangelo.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through Prati neighborhood — Rome's laid-back residential quarter near the Vatican. Browse the local shops on Via Cola di Rienzo. Enjoy a gelato from a neighborhood gelateria (avoid tourist traps; look for 'artigianale' signs, ~€2.50).

meals.breakfast: Bar/café near the hotel — classic Roman breakfast of espresso + cornetto (~€2–3). Try 'Bar San Pietro' on Via della Conciliazione.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or grab food from a nearby alimentari before entering the museums. Eat in the Vatican Museums' internal courtyard café to save time, or buy a panino outside (~€5–7).
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — a beloved local trattoria offering a fixed-price Roman menu (cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara) for around €15–18 per person including wine. Book ahead or arrive early.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be booked online in advance — last-minute tickets are often unavailable or overpriced through touts. Dress code required for the Basilica: no bare shoulders or knees. Bring a scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line A from Ottaviano to Spagna (10 min, ~€1.50). Visit the Spanish Steps (free) early in the morning when they're nearly empty. Walk down to the Trevi Fountain (free) — throw a coin for good luck. Continue on foot to the Pantheon (~15 min walk). Entry to the Pantheon is €5 — one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings and absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market (open until ~2:00 PM, free to browse). Grab lunch here. Afterward, walk to the nearby Piazza Navona (free) — admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and the lively street artists. Continue to the Palazzo Altemps (part of the National Roman Museum, €10 combined ticket) for a superb, uncrowded collection of ancient sculpture in a stunning Renaissance palace.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Via del Governo Vecchio — one of Rome's most atmospheric antique and vintage streets. Enjoy aperitivo hour (5:00–8:00 PM) at a local bar; many offer free snacks with a €5–7 Aperol Spritz or glass of wine. End the evening with a passeggiata (evening stroll) back through the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Café near Spagna metro — try a local bar away from the tourist strip for espresso and cornetto (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Campo de' Fiori market — buy fresh fruit, a slice of focaccia, and local cheese for a self-assembled picnic (~€6–8). Eat on the piazza steps.
meals.dinner: Osteria da Fortunata near Campo de' Fiori — famous for handmade pasta at honest prices. Cacio e pepe or carbonara ~€10–12 per plate. Simple, authentic, and beloved by locals.

day_by_day.notes: The historic center is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes. Avoid overpriced restaurants directly on Piazza Navona or near the Trevi Fountain. Walk one block away for much better value. Stay hydrated — Rome has free drinking fountains ('nasoni') throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Take Bus 40 or 64 from near the Vatican to Largo Argentina (free ancient Roman ruins, open-air cat sanctuary — free). Walk to the Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) — designed by Michelangelo. Visit the Capitoline Museums (~€15), Rome's oldest public museums with masterpieces including the original Marcus Aurelius statue, Capitoline Wolf, and stunning views over the Roman Forum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the Capitoline Hill to the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill (combined ticket with Colosseum ~€18 — book online to skip lines). Spend 2–3 hours walking through the heart of ancient Rome: the Sacred Way, Temple of Saturn, Arch of Titus, and the palaces of the emperors on Palatine Hill. The Colosseum exterior is visible from Palatine Hill at no extra cost if budget is tight, or enter for the full experience (included in combined ticket).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic working-class foodie district. Visit the Testaccio Market (closes at 3:00 PM but the neighborhood is lively all evening). Walk up Monte Testaccio — a hill made entirely of ancient amphora shards — for a quirky free experience.

meals.breakfast: Quick espresso and pastry at a local bar near the hotel (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Supplì Roma near Largo Argentina — try the iconic Roman street food supplì (fried rice balls with tomato and mozzarella, ~€2 each) and grab a slice of pizza al taglio. Lunch for ~€6–8.
meals.dinner: Testaccio market area — try 'Da Remo' for Rome's best thin-crust pizza in a no-frills, cash-only trattoria. Pizza from €7–9, beer €3. Expect a wait but worth every minute.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum/Forum tickets online at least 2–3 days in advance — they frequently sell out. The combined ticket is valid for 2 consecutive days, so you can split the visit if needed. Testaccio is authentic Rome — avoid tourist menus here and order like a local.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's most spectacular art collections (Bernini sculptures, Caravaggio paintings, Raphael). Admission is €15 but MANDATORY reservation required (timed entry, 2-hour slots). Book online well in advance. Take Bus 910 or Metro A to Flaminio then walk through Villa Borghese park (~20 min). The park itself is free and beautiful for a morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in Villa Borghese park (free) — rent a rowboat on the small lake (~€3/person), visit the free Pincio Terrace for panoramic views over Rome, and relax in the shade. Walk down the Spanish Steps from the top (Via Trinità dei Monti) for a different perspective. Browse the boutiques and street vendors on Via del Corso (free to window-shop).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Trastevere neighborhood — Rome's most romantic and bohemian quarter. Cross the Tiber via Ponte Sisto (beautiful pedestrian bridge) and wander the cobblestone lanes. Visit the free Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere — glittering 12th-century gold mosaics lit up beautifully at night (free). Enjoy the lively piazza atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or grab a maritozzo (cream-filled bun) — a Roman breakfast specialty (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — buy supplies from a nearby alimentari or Mercato Trionfale (Rome's largest covered market, near the Vatican, ~€7–9 for bread, cheese, prosciutto, fruit)
meals.dinner: Trastevere dinner at 'Da Enzo al 29' — a tiny, beloved trattoria with Roman classics. Arrive early (7:00 PM) or expect a wait. Pasta dishes ~€10–13, house wine €4/glass. Budget ~€20–25 total.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is non-negotiable for art lovers but the reservation system is strict — you must book weeks ahead in peak season. Trastevere gets very lively on Friday nights — great for people-watching but restaurants fill up fast. Book dinner or arrive at opening time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (free) — Rome's cathedral and the oldest Christian basilica in the world, often overlooked by tourists. Take Metro A to San Giovanni. Also visit the adjacent Scala Santa (Holy Stairs, free) — pilgrims climb on their knees. Continue to the nearby Basilica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme (free) — contains relics of the True Cross and beautiful frescoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Aventine Hill — a peaceful, leafy residential neighborhood. Visit the famous Knights of Malta Keyhole on Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta (free) — peer through the keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Walk through the beautiful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci, free) for sweeping views of Rome. Visit the Basilica di Santa Sabina (free) — one of Rome's oldest and most serene churches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Trastevere/Gianicolo area. Climb the Janiculum Hill (Gianicolo) for the best panoramic view of Rome's skyline — completely free and stunning at sunset. A cannon is fired here daily at noon (free spectacle). Enjoy a relaxed final Saturday evening stroll back through Trastevere or Prati.

meals.breakfast: Local bar near hotel — espresso, cornetto, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Near the Aventine — 'Volpetti Più' in Testaccio (a short walk) for a self-service tavola calda (hot food buffet). Load up a tray with Roman classics for ~€10–12. Excellent quality.
meals.dinner: Cook-at-home or grab takeaway — visit the Mercato Trionfale near the hotel for fresh pasta, sauces, and local wine. Cook a simple meal in the hotel if facilities allow, or assemble a picnic-style dinner (~€10–12 for two). Alternatively, return to a favorite restaurant from earlier in the week.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is market day across Rome — Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere runs Sunday mornings (see Day 7). The Aventine Hill is very quiet and peaceful — a great contrast to the busy tourist sites. Gianicolo sunset is one of Rome's great free experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the Porta Portese Flea Market (7:00 AM – 2:00 PM, free entry) in Trastevere — Rome's legendary Sunday market with antiques, vintage clothing, art prints, and local crafts. Perfect for budget souvenirs and people-watching. Haggling is expected and encouraged.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon: revisit any favorite spots or tick off remaining items. Consider the free Basilica di San Clemente near the Colosseum — three layers of history stacked underground (free basilica, small fee for underground excavations ~€10). Or simply return to the Prati neighborhood near the hotel for a final gelato and coffee on Via Cola di Rienzo. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in the Prati neighborhood — a relaxed, local area with excellent value restaurants. Enjoy a proper sit-down Roman farewell meal. Reflect on the week over a carafe of house wine.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the Porta Portese market or a nearby bar in Trastevere (~€3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel — a slice of pizza al taglio and a cold drink from a local forno (bakery) in Prati (~€5–7). Save appetite for a proper farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: 'Osteria dell'Angelo' or 'Trattoria Settimio all'Arancio' in Prati for a memorable final Roman dinner. Order the full experience: antipasto, pasta, secondi, and house wine. Budget ~€25–30 for a splurge-worthy farewell meal — still excellent value by any standard.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is cash only — bring small bills. Keep an eye on belongings in crowded market areas. If departing by flight, check transfer time to the airport: Fiumicino requires ~1 hour travel + 2 hours check-in. Plan your final day around your departure logistics. Rome's tap water is safe and delicious — refill bottles at any nasone fountain to save money all week.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight lands at 13:00, so use the morning slot for travel. Take the Leonardo Express from Fiumicino to Roma Termini, then connect to the Borgo district. Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and get oriented in the Vatican neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk — Stroll through the Borgo district and along the Tiber River. Cross the Sant'Angelo Bridge for stunning views of Castel Sant'Angelo, explore the surrounding piazzas, and get a feel for your home base. Pop into a local alimentari to pick up snacks and water for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Head across the river to Trastevere (15-min walk or short bus ride) for this guided evening experience through cobblestone streets. Sample supplì, cacio e pepe bites, and local wines as you soak up the neighborhood's vibrant atmosphere at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick espresso and cornetto at a bar near Fiumicino airport or Roma Termini while in transit.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel after check-in — try Pizzarium Bonci on Via della Meloria for exceptional Roman pizza al taglio (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Included tastings on the Trastevere Food & Wine Walk; supplement with a sit-down glass of wine at Enoteca Ferrara in Trastevere (€8–12 per glass).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed given the 13:00 arrival. Pre-book the Trastevere Food Walk in advance as evening slots fill quickly in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes from the start.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Start early with a pre-booked skip-the-line ticket (9:00 AM entry recommended). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Being steps from your hotel is a huge advantage.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Square — After the Museums, walk directly into St. Peter's Square (free entry to the Basilica). Climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Take your time in the Basilica admiring Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's towering baldachin.
day_by_day.evening: Prati District Dinner & Evening Stroll — The upscale Prati neighborhood, just north of the Vatican, is perfect for an evening out. Browse Via Cola di Rienzo for gelato and aperitivo, then settle in for a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or at a nearby café — a classic Roman breakfast of espresso, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a warm cornetto (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch inside or near the Vatican Museums — Il Sorpasso in Prati offers excellent Roman classics like tonnarelli cacio e pepe in a relaxed setting (€15–20).
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — a beloved neighborhood trattoria serving traditional Roman cucina like rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio. Fixed-price dinner around €25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead for June dates. Dress code applies for St. Peter's — shoulders and knees must be covered. Arrive at the Museums at opening time to beat the heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Tour — Take the tram or bus to the Testaccio neighborhood (25 mins from Borgo) for this immersive morning market experience. Sample aged pecorino romano, seasonal Roman vegetables, supplì, and artisan charcuterie while learning about authentic Roman food culture from local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Visit — After the market, walk to the nearby Colosseum area. Purchase a combined ticket (€18) covering the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Spend the afternoon exploring the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, timing your visit to catch the late afternoon golden light on the ancient ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo & Dinner in Testaccio — Return to Testaccio, Rome's culinary heartland, for dinner. The neighborhood is authentic, local, and perfectly suited to a mid-range food lover's budget.

meals.breakfast: Included tastings at the Testaccio Market Culinary Tour — this IS the morning meal experience.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Testaccio after the tour — Flavio al Velavevodetto is a Roman institution serving hearty pasta dishes with a view of Monte Testaccio (€18–25).
meals.dinner: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina near Campo de' Fiori — world-class Roman ingredients crafted into unforgettable dishes. Book ahead; budget €35–45 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Monday–Saturday mornings only; it closes around 2:00 PM. Wear sunscreen and a hat — June afternoons at the Forum can be very sunny and exposed. Book Roscioli well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese park for your timed-entry visit to the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly by reservation, 2-hour slots). Marvel at Bernini's Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina, and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in an intimate, crowd-controlled setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Park & Pincian Hill Terrace — After the gallery, enjoy a relaxed afternoon in the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€5), stroll the shaded paths, and walk to the Pincian Hill terrace for one of Rome's best panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Piazza del Popolo & Flaminio Neighborhood — Descend from the Pincian Hill into Piazza del Popolo to explore the twin baroque churches and the piazza itself. Enjoy aperitivo in the lively Flaminio area before heading back toward the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — try Sciascia Caffè in Prati, one of Rome's legendary espresso bars, for a perfect morning coffee and pastry (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese — pick up supplies beforehand from a Prati deli: fresh bread, prosciutto, mozzarella, and fruit. Enjoy it on the grass (€12–15 total, very mid-range).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso in Prati for a more relaxed evening — excellent natural wines, creative bruschette, and Roman-inspired small plates (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked in advance — they sell out weeks ahead in summer. The gallery only admits visitors in 2-hour timed slots with no exceptions. Arrive 15 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Pantheon & Historic Center — Walk or take a short bus ride to the ancient Pantheon (book timed entry online, €5). Spend time inside this perfectly preserved 2,000-year-old temple, then explore the surrounding piazzas — Piazza della Rotonda, Piazza Navona (Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers), and the charming streets in between.
day_by_day.afternoon: Campo de' Fiori & Jewish Ghetto Art Walk — Browse the afternoon market at Campo de' Fiori, then walk into Rome's historic Jewish Ghetto. Explore the Portico d'Ottavia ruins, visit the Great Synagogue exterior, and discover the neighborhood's layered history. Stop into small galleries along Via del Governo Vecchio for contemporary Roman art.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Dinner & Nightlife — Cross back to Trastevere for a proper sit-down dinner in one of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhoods, then enjoy an evening stroll through its illuminated medieval streets.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto in Trastevere or a café near the hotel — espresso and pastry (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Piazza Navona — Osteria del Pegno offers traditional Roman pasta in a historic setting at reasonable prices (€18–25).
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a beloved, no-frills Roman trattoria with exceptional cacio e pepe, carbonara, and coda alla vaccinara. Book ahead; €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now requires advance ticket booking. June midday heat in the historic center can be intense — schedule the outdoor walking portions for early morning or after 5:00 PM when possible.

day_by_day.morning: Capitoline Museums — Rome's oldest public museums sit atop Capitoline Hill with sweeping views of the Roman Forum below. Explore extraordinary ancient sculpture including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning Renaissance art collections. Budget 2.5–3 hours (€15 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Aventine Hill & Orange Garden — Walk up the scenic Aventine Hill to the Giardino degli Aranci (Orange Garden) for one of Rome's most romantic panoramic views. Seek out the famous Knights of Malta keyhole on Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta — peer through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Visit the early Christian Basilica di Santa Sabina.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Aperitivo & Special Dinner — Celebrate your penultimate evening in Rome with a proper aperitivo hour at a rooftop or terrace bar, followed by a slightly elevated dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Caffè della Pace near Piazza Navona — a beautifully frescoed historic café perfect for a leisurely morning coffee (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Quick and excellent lunch at Supplì Roma near the Capitoline — Rome's best supplì (fried risotto balls) and pizza al taglio (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Osteria Fernanda in Trastevere/Monteverde — a creative, modern Roman restaurant with a strong focus on seasonal ingredients and natural wine. A slight step up for a special evening (€40–50 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: The Capitoline Museums are closed on Mondays — verify the day of the week before finalizing this plan. The Knights of Malta keyhole is free and magical at any time of day. The Orange Garden is best visited in late afternoon for golden light views.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in the Borgo & Vatican Neighborhood — Use your last morning to revisit your home neighborhood with fresh eyes. Walk along the Tiber, cross back over Sant'Angelo Bridge, and browse the Borgo Pio street for last-minute souvenirs — artisan food shops selling Roman pasta, olive oil, and wine make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Castel Sant'Angelo Interior Visit — If not yet explored, visit the interior of Castel Sant'Angelo (€15) — Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress. Climb to the rooftop terrace for sweeping views over Rome and the Tiber, and explore the fascinating papal apartments and armory within.
day_by_day.evening: Final Dinner & Departure Prep — Enjoy a relaxed final dinner near the hotel, pack your bags, and prepare for departure. Reflect on a week of extraordinary art, food, and Roman history.

meals.breakfast: A final proper Roman breakfast at your favorite neighborhood bar — make it count with a perfectly pulled espresso and a warm cornetto alla crema (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Angelo or Pizzarium Bonci in Prati — a fitting farewell to the neighborhood that hosted you all week (€15–20).
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a trusted Prati trattoria — Trattoria Settimio all'Arancio or a return to a favorite spot from the week. Keep it relaxed and savory (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early on June 22, pack bags the night before and arrange an early taxi or airport shuttle. The Leonardo Express runs from Roma Termini to Fiumicino every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes. Leave at least 2.5–3 hours before flight time.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer from Fiumicino Airport to your boutique stay in the Borgo district, Vatican City. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome Prosecco prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely Borgo Neighbourhood Stroll — After settling in, take a gentle self-guided walk through the historic Borgo Pio pedestrian street, just steps from the hotel. Browse artisan shops, admire the Castel Sant'Angelo from the Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge, and soak in your first views of St. Peter's Square at golden-hour light.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner at Il Sorpasso or Ristorante Il Matriciano — Two acclaimed neighbourhood classics within easy walking distance of the Borgo. Opt for Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi) for old-school Roman elegance: cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and a curated regional wine list in a refined, intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival) — light snack on board or at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick artisan sandwich and a glass of Frascati at Forno Roscioli or a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi 55) — classic Roman cuisine, white-tablecloth service, extensive Italian wine cellar. Budget approx. €80–120 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in when booking to ensure the room is ready upon 14:30–15:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (Private Early-Access Tour) — Begin with an exclusive pre-opening guided tour (07:00–09:00) before the general public enters. Walk through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminate in a near-empty Sistine Chapel to fully absorb Michelangelo's masterpiece ceiling and The Last Judgment in tranquil silence. Your hotel's concierge can arrange a certified art historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — After the museums, cross into the Basilica for a guided tour of Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's monumental baldachin, and the papal tombs. Ascend the dome for panoramic views over Rome's rooftops. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo & Fine Dining at Settimio all'Arancio or Ristorante Antico Arco — Head to the Janiculum Hill area for Antico Arco, one of Rome's most celebrated fine-dining destinations. Creative Roman cuisine, exceptional tasting menus, and a world-class wine list in a candlelit 17th-century setting.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — freshly baked cornetti, seasonal fruit, cappuccino, and cold cuts served before the early museum departure.
meals.lunch: Osteria dell'Angelo (Via G. Bettolo) — authentic Roman trattoria beloved by locals, a short walk from the Vatican. Fixed lunch menu featuring rigatoni all'amatriciana and abbacchio. Approx. €35–50 per person.
meals.dinner: Antico Arco (Piazzale Aurelio 7, Janiculum) — tasting menu €95–130 per person, wine pairing available. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Private Vatican early-access tours must be booked weeks ahead. Dress code for the Basilica: covered shoulders and knees. Comfortable walking shoes essential for cobblestone Vatican grounds.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience (Private Guided Visit) — Take a private car (15-minute ride) to the Villa Borghese. Timed-entry tickets are mandatory; a private art historian guide elevates the experience. Marvel at Bernini's Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina, and Caravaggio's dramatic Boy with a Fruit Basket and David with the Head of Goliath. Maximum 2-hour visit per the gallery's strict policy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill Terrace — After the gallery, stroll through the manicured gardens, rent a rowboat on the lake, or simply relax in the shade. Walk to the Pincian Hill terrace for one of Rome's finest panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and the city skyline. Optional: visit the twin baroque churches below in the piazza.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join a premium small-group or private evening food tour through Trastevere's cobblestone alleys. Sample supplì (Roman fried rice balls), artisan pizza al taglio, pecorino romano, local wine, and finish with a classic maritozzo pastry. The neighbourhood's lantern-lit ambiance at dusk is magical.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — full Italian breakfast with fresh orange juice, yogurt, pastries, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Caffè delle Arti inside the Villa Borghese grounds — elegant terrace dining with Roman and Mediterranean cuisine. Approx. €50–70 per person.
meals.dinner: Integrated into the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (premium private tour includes tastings). Supplement with a sit-down finale at Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — beloved for cacio e pepe and tiramisù. Approx. €45–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery limits visitors to 360 per 2-hour slot — book tickets and private guide at least 4–6 weeks in advance. Wear comfortable shoes for the evening Trastevere walk on uneven cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Tour — Private car to the Testaccio neighbourhood for an immersive morning market experience. A local food expert guide leads you through Rome's most authentic covered market (Mercato di Testaccio). Taste aged pecorino, cured meats, seasonal produce, freshly fried filetti di baccalà, and artisan cheeses. Learn the history of Rome's 'fifth quarter' cuisine from the nearby former slaughterhouse district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Guided Visit — A short walk from Testaccio, enter the Palatine Hill and Roman Forum with a private archaeologist guide. Explore the ruins of imperial palaces, the Temple of Saturn, and the Arch of Titus. Linger for the spectacular views over the Forum below. Finish at the Colosseum exterior for iconic photographs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Aperitivo & Gourmet Dinner — Return to the hotel to freshen up, then head to a rooftop bar (Hotel Raphael or Il Sorpasso terrace) for Negroni cocktails and cicchetti with views. Dinner at Ristorante Pipero Roma (near Campo de' Fiori) — one of Rome's Michelin-starred destinations, celebrated for refined modern Roman cuisine and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Light in-hotel breakfast before the early market tour.
meals.lunch: Integrated tastings during the Testaccio Market Tour. Supplement at Flavio al Velavevodetto — a Testaccio institution built into the Monte dei Cocci hill, serving exceptional coda alla vaccinara and rigatoni con pajata. Approx. €40–60 per person.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pipero Roma (Corso Vittorio Emanuele II 246) — tasting menu €120–160 per person, wine pairing recommended. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is liveliest before noon — aim for a 09:00 start. Combined Colosseum/Forum/Palatine tickets can be upgraded to include priority access. June heat can be intense in the afternoon; bring water and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Capitoline Museums Private Tour — Rome's oldest public museums sit atop the Capitoline Hill, designed by Michelangelo. A private guide unveils the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping terraced views over the Roman Forum. Explore the pinacoteca (art gallery) featuring Caravaggio's St. John the Baptist and works by Titian and Rubens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pantheon, Piazza Navona & Luxury Shopping — Walk to the perfectly preserved Pantheon (reserve timed entry) and stand beneath its unreinforced concrete dome, still the world's largest after 2,000 years. Stroll to Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Browse luxury boutiques along Via Condotti and Via Borgognona — Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi — for optional shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking Class & Private Dinner — A premium hands-on Roman cooking class in a private kitchen near the city centre (offered by Walks of Italy or a private chef). Learn to make fresh pasta, cacio e pepe, and a classic tiramisu, then sit down to enjoy the meal you've prepared with paired wines. Alternatively, dine at La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel) — Rome's only 3-Michelin-star restaurant, with unparalleled city views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — leisurely full breakfast.
meals.lunch: Ristorante La Rosetta (Via della Rosetta 9) — Rome's finest seafood restaurant near the Pantheon, beloved for its raw bar and grilled branzino. Approx. €80–110 per person.
meals.dinner: Private cooking class dinner (included in class fee, approx. €150–200 per person) OR La Pergola (Via Alberto Cadlolo 101) — tasting menu €250–300 per person, dress code strictly enforced, reserve months ahead.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola reservations should ideally be made 2–3 months in advance. The Pantheon now charges a timed-entry fee (€5); book online. Via Condotti boutiques are open 10:00–19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj Private Collection — One of Rome's best-kept secrets: a still-inhabited aristocratic palace whose private art gallery houses Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X, Caravaggio's Rest on the Flight to Egypt, and works by Raphael and Titian. An audio guide narrated by the current Prince Doria Pamphilj adds an intimate personal touch. Arrive early to beat weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Janiculum Hill & Trastevere Leisure Afternoon — Take a short drive up to the Janiculum Hill for Rome's most expansive panoramic viewpoint. Watch the traditional noon cannon fire (if timing aligns). Descend into Trastevere for a leisurely afternoon: explore the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere, browse artisan leather and ceramics shops, and relax at a shaded café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Aperitivo & Special Dinner — Sunset Negroni on the terrace of your boutique hotel or at Castel Sant'Angelo's café with direct views of the illuminated fortress. Farewell dinner at Glass Hostaria (Trastevere) — a sleek Michelin-starred restaurant offering avant-garde interpretations of Roman cuisine in a contemporary glass-and-steel interior, a stunning contrast to the medieval neighbourhood outside.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel — full Italian breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tonnarello (Trastevere) or Grazia & Graziella — charming neighbourhood trattorias with outdoor seating, excellent cacio e pepe and abbacchio. Approx. €35–55 per person.
meals.dinner: Glass Hostaria (Vicolo del Cinque 58, Trastevere) — tasting menu €95–130 per person, wine pairing available. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is closed Thursdays. Saturday in Trastevere is lively and atmospheric but can be crowded by evening — dinner reservation essential. The Janiculum cannon fires at 12:00 daily.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at St. Peter's Square & Final Vatican Moments — Wake early for a contemplative walk to an almost-empty St. Peter's Square at sunrise — one of Rome's most magical experiences. If Sunday timing aligns, attend the Papal Angelus blessing at 12:00 (the Pope appears at his window overlooking the square). Browse the weekly Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (07:00–14:00) for antiques and curios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Castel Sant'Angelo Museum — Your hotel's prime location makes this a perfect final visit. Explore the former mausoleum of Emperor Hadrian, converted into a papal fortress and prison. Climb to the top terrace for sweeping views of the Tiber, St. Peter's dome, and the city — a fitting final panorama of Rome. Leisurely hotel check-out and luggage storage arranged with concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Lunch & Departure Transfer — Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell lunch before your departure. Private chauffeur transfer to Fiumicino Airport arranged by the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Early light in-hotel breakfast before the sunrise walk — fresh fruit, cornetto, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio (Via dell'Arancio 50) — a refined, timeless Roman restaurant near the Castel Sant'Angelo, celebrated for its seasonal tasting menus and warm hospitality. Approx. €70–100 per person. Linger over dessert and digestivi.
meals.dinner: Not applicable — departure day. Pack artisan food souvenirs (aged pecorino, pasta, bottarga) from the Testaccio Market or Roscioli delicatessen for a taste of Rome at home.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before scheduled departure. Porta Portese market runs Sunday mornings only — go early for the best finds. Ask the hotel concierge to prepare a curated list of Roman food shops for last-minute gourmet souvenirs.
